title: רב ספרא
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs:
(a) God-fearing; Bava Batra 88a says he fulfilled “speaks truth in his heart.” Heilprin connects this with a donkey incident. Bava Kamma 116a: a miracle occurred on a journey with many people. A lion accompanied them; each day one threw it a donkey to eat. On Rav Safra's turn it refused his donkey, apparently because he did not covet its value. I do not know the donkey matter. Rashbam, Bava Batra 88a, and Rashi, Makkot 24a, give the account. Rashi cites Rav Aḥai Gaon’s She’iltot: Safra recited Shema when a buyer offered a price for his merchandise. He remained silent; the buyer thought the price too low and increased it. After prayer Safra accepted only the original offer, having resolved inwardly to sell for it. Menorat HaMaor [source מ״מ, gate 4, folio 33, first account and foliation uncollated], tells it differently, apparently an error; see there.

Menorat HaMaor also tells of Rav Safra walking outside town with students. A pious man thought he had come to greet him and asked why he had troubled himself. R. Safra said he had come for a walk. His students asked why he said this; he refused to lie. They suggested silence; he said silence would not fulfill speaking truth in his heart. End of quotation. See Ḥullin 94b; I think that Gemara is intended, but it differs; see there. Safra singed an animal's head for Shabbat, Shabbat 119a. He was a bachelor living in a city, Pesaḥim 113a (Arvei Pesaḥim) and Kiddushin. R. Abbahu praised him to sectarians as great, Avodah Zarah 4a.

(b) R. Ḥiyya said: R. Safra said in the name of someone of Rabbi's household, Berakhot 34b. Beit Yosef, Oraḥ Ḥayyim 101, has this reading. Heilprin identifies him as R. Naḥman son of Rabbi; Halikhot Olam also gives the household reading and identifies him as Rabban Gamliel. Heilprin also cites Keritot, Yemot Olam, gate 3 §20; see above, DeBei. Asheri reads someone of R. Yannai's household; Rif, someone of R. Ammi's, omitting 'R. Ḥiyya said.' He and Rava visited Mar Yuḥana bar Ḥana—some say Mar Yuḥana son of Rav Ḥana bar Bizna—who prepared an egla tilta [a calf either a third grown or the third calf born, according to interpretations recorded by Rashi]. Rava asked his attendant to acquire the priestly gifts for him. Rava ate; Safra did not. In a dream they recited to Safra, 'One who removes a garment,' etc. He asked Rav Yosef whether this was for violating the master's teaching. Yosef said it referred to Rava; why not recite it to Rava? Rava was under rebuke (see his entry).

Safra entered a privy; Rav Aḥa came and snorted (R. Abba in the checked Berakhot 62b text). R. Safra left the Land accompanied by Rav Huna and Rav Kahana son of Rav Iki, Pesaḥim 52b; should read R. Huna son of Rav Iki, and R. Kahana. Rav Yosef applied 'He asks his wood, and his staff tells him,' there. His father asked R. Zeira, Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:4:6. He said to Rava, “Moshe, have you spoken well?” (Shabbat 101b). Ḥullin 93a: R. Abba says, etc.; R. Safra says, 'Moshe'—Rashi: Torah scholar—Rava says, 'Moshe,' etc. He partnered with Issur, dividing without Issur's knowledge; before Rabbah son of Rav Huna, Abaye cited R. Yosef bar Minyomi reporting R. Naḥman, Bava Metzia 31b–32a. Bava Batra 144a: his father left money; he traded with it, and his brothers sued before Rava. At his death Abaye ordered garment-tearing because his teachings were heard daily in the study house. Abaye told R. Safra, 'When you go up,' etc.; he found R. Zerika, Ḥullin 110b.

(c) R. Abba said; he objected to R. Abba, who sent him to collect from Rav Yosef bar Ḥama (Bava Kamma 104b). Abba bar Marta; R. Abbahu; R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa; R. Ḥanina bar Pappa. R. Safra said R. Abbahu related, Berakhot 63a. He spoke to Abaye, Bekhorot 4a; Abaye questioned him in Yoma 11a; Eruvin 45b; he objected to Abaye. Abaye told Rav Yosef, “Thus R. Safra said” (Eruvin 103a). He spoke to R. Oshaya. Rav Aḥa; Rav Aḥa bar Yosef; Rav Aḥa son of Rav Huna. Issur partnered with him (see above), and Issur the convert. R. Ammi said: R. Yoḥanan said, Shabbat 5b; Eruvin 20b. Rav Dimi, his brother; Rav Dimi bar Ḥinena; Rav Huna bar Ḥanina; Rav Huna son of Rav Ika (see above). R. Zeira said: R. Safra said: R. Hamnuna said, Ḥullin 80a (source 70a). R. Zerika (see above). R. Ḥiyya of Ctesiphon said. R. Ḥiyya said: Rav Safra said, Berakhot 34b, as in שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas]; I do not know which R. Ḥiyya (see above). R. Safra said: R. Ḥiyya said, Shabbat 37a. In R. Yehoshua ben Ḥananyah's name, Kiddushin 30a—requires examination, since he was much earlier. In R. Yehoshua of the South's name, Avodah Zarah 30b. Mar Yuḥana bar Ḥana. R. Yoḥanan said, Sanhedrin 31b. R. Yoḥanan, his brother. Rav Kahana. Rav Naḥman (see below). Avira related to him. He raised a contradiction before Rava, Pesaḥim 59b; Rav there is a scribal error, as Yalkut, Pinḥas§782 also shows. Rav Kahana before Rabbah (see his entry). Rava said Rav Safra got the better of three ordained rabbis (Gittin 29b) (see R. Abba bar Marta). Rabbah calls him 'our colleague R. Safra,' Shabbat 124a. Rabbah son of Rav Huna (see above); Rami bar Ḥama. R. Sheshet told R. Naḥman, 'Safra your colleague,' Bekhorot 10b.
